detail: one-world makes each generic include and attach its implementation (history-paged, catalog-paged, payload-arena-extent), so every implementation closure's exported vocabulary enters every includer's world: measured (FAM5.md (c)) 23-36% of each closure's enabled runes reach typical consumers (catalog-logic +4,278 enabled runes, served-columns +6,629, owner-served-carried +847), the source of five rule families of reds (NTH openers, slice inverse, adt size/serialization, recognizer bridge, live-link backchaining). Landing: each implementation book exports only what attach-stobj and the generic's correspondence need; everything else LOCAL. Measure: FAM5 (c) goes to ~0 at the three consumers; the per-rule census enables and the defthmd rules introduced for one-world are deleted where they become unnecessary. G4: a deletion landing (local-ising exports, removing census enables and their script). G8: removes the whole class of include-order reds that the export leak causes. Main 10-14: A's next landing after one-world (C18).
title: one-world B: implementation books export only what their attach needs; internal vocabulary LOCAL
